A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 34-page KatFishNet study, including Appendices A–R. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the only visible difference is the arXiv version/date stamp on page 1.

before.justification: v4 reports original detection experiments in Section 5/Table 3, supplementary linguistic and robustness analyses, and an expert evaluation of 75 texts by three evaluators in Appendix R.

after.justification: v5 retains the original detection experiments in Section 5/Table 3 and all supplementary empirical results, including the expert evaluation in Appendix R.

M1.justification: KatFishNet's spacing, POS-combination and punctuation features, classifiers, and feature-ensemble procedure are identical in Section 3 and Appendices H–K.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same KatFish essays, poetry and paper abstracts from humans and four LLMs. Unseen-generator evaluation, human-style revision scenarios and expert-evaluation coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Section 4.2/Table 3 retain identical confidence-based, perturbation-based, Exaone 3.5 paraphrasing/prompting and RoBERTa comparisons. Comparator membership also matches throughout the appendices.

E3.justification: Both retain AUC-ROC evaluation, the 80:20 human-text split, GPT-4o training data and Solar/Qwen2/Llama3.1 test sets. Appendix prompting, robustness and expert-evaluation protocols are also identical.

E4.justification: The linguistic analyses, classifier and feature-ensemble comparisons, knowledge-guided prompting, human-style imitation robustness test, and expert evaluation are all retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both report averages over five experiments in Tables 3, 9 and 13 and identical mean/standard-deviation reporting for Eojeol counts in Table 7. No statistical or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 3 retains punctuation-based average AUC-ROC values of 94.88, 73.10 and 75.62 for essays, poetry and abstracts, respectively.

T1.justification: Feature definitions in Section 3 and the appendices, along with the Zipf/Heaps-law discussion in Appendix Q, are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about KatFish's novelty, Korean-specific detection, punctuation-feature effectiveness and the reported 19.78% average AUC-ROC advantage.

C2.justification: Explanations involving Korean writing conventions and multilingual training are unchanged. The limitations concerning genre coverage, mixed human/LLM text and morphological-analyzer accuracy are also identical.

D1.justification: Generation prompts, implementation details, five-epoch RoBERTa fine-tuning, RTX A6000 hardware disclosure and code/data access information remain identical, including Appendices C and I.

R1.justification: Section 6, Appendix L and the reference list are unchanged, including the positioning against M4GT-Bench and MULTITuDE and the motivation for Korean-specific detection.

P1.justification: Only the marginal arXiv identifier/date changes from v4, 2 Jul 2025, to v5, 19 Sep 2025. Article wording, headings and section/appendix order are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions and their placement are identical. Rendered pages 2–34 match pixel-for-pixel; page 1 differs only in the administrative version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The main text and appendices retain identical scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations and reproducibility information. Updating only the arXiv version/date stamp produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
